title: Block periodization of endurance training – a systematic review and meta-analysis
publisher: Open Access Journal of Sports Medicine
claims: A total of 2905 records were screened and 20 studies met the eligibility criteria.
Six studies were pooled for meta-analysis of maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max) and maximal power output (Wmax).

Block periodization showed small favorable effects compared with traditional periodization for VO2max (standardized mean difference 0.40; 95% CI 0.02, 0.79) and Wmax (standardized mean difference 0.28; 95% CI 0.01, 0.54).
For endurance performance and workload at different exercise thresholds, block periodization generally showed moderate- to large-effect sizes compared with traditional periodization.
The authors caution that the results come from small studies with generally low methodological quality, with a mean PEDro score of 3.7/10.
